colibri 2.2.0: everything since 2.1.0 (2026-10-31). The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri/blob/v2.2.0/CHANGELOG.md).

## New models

- **Inkling-2-Small** (594B, 17B active, Apache 2.0): text, pictures and tools, from unsloth's GGUFs (UD-IQ1_S 171.7 GB to UD-Q4_K_XL 354 GB, pictures through the mmproj) or our int4 g64 converted from the NVFP4 release; CUDA and Vulkan, an MTP drafter (`INK2_MTP=1`).
- **Inkling-2-Mini** (26.4B, 3.4B active, Apache 2.0), whose middle layers run three passes: text and pictures from unsloth's GGUFs (UD-IQ2_XXS 8.5 GB to UD-Q4_K_XL 17.6 GB; their root files and the `Mainline_Support` ones, mainline llama.cpp's `inkling2_loop` layout, alike) or our int4 g64 from the NVFP4 release; Vulkan and CUDA with a decode step in one frame of their dense chains (the routed experts on the card, the attention split over its positions), and the CPU. UD-Q4_K_XL decodes at 40.9-41.1 tok/s with CUDA, 39.2-39.4 with Vulkan and 8.0-8.1 on the CPU, and reads a 570-token prompt at 285-289 tok/s with CUDA and 270-277 with Vulkan.
- **Qwen3.8-27B** (dense): text and images on CUDA, Vulkan and the CPU, its MTP head from a GGUF, and speculative decoding on CUDA with DFlash2.
- **Kimi K3.1 Pro**: K3's weights with sparse attention past 2048 tokens, on the CPU, Vulkan and a new CUDA chain.
- **Qwen-Image-2.1 from GGUFs**, base and Turbo: about 10 GB on disk and a 5.9 GB RAM peak, where the official checkpoint is 33 GB.
- **DeepSeek V4.1 Flash** on Vulkan and CUDA, **GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash** on the CUDA chain, **Qwen3.8 with AMD Quark's MXFP4 experts** (CPU).

## Faster

Measured for this release, 2.1.0 against it, through `coli serve` on an RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell (24 GB) with an i5-13500 and 62 GB; prompt in tok/s at 1000 tokens, then 300 tokens of decode, two runs each:

| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ2_XS | Vulkan | 127 -> 135-137 | 34.7 -> 36.3-36.7 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ3_XXS | CUDA | 27-28 -> 478-492 | 10.5-15.9 -> 41.5-41.6 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ3_XXS | Vulkan | 173-174 -> 276 | 30.7-31.8 -> 33.0-33.4 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash UD-IQ2_XXS | CUDA | 4.2-5.3 -> 17.1-17.5 | 1.9-2.3 -> 5.2 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash UD-IQ2_XXS | Vulkan | 16.1-16.2 -> 17.5-17.7 | 4.7 -> 5.5-5.6 |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash UD-IQ1_S | CUDA | 16.3-16.4 -> 18.3-18.6 | 6.1-6.2 -> 6.1 |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash UD-IQ1_S | Vulkan | 19.2-20.3 -> 21.5-22.0 | 5.8-6.0 -> 6.4-6.5 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M | CUDA | 3297-3436 -> 3278-3419 | 102.1-104.4 -> 104.4-106.2 |

On the CPU (Ryzen 7 PRO 8700GE, 8 cores), the GGUF kernels' new forms (#2868): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-IQ2_XXS reads a 500-token prompt at 148-149 tok/s instead of 125-126 and decodes at 25.9-27.0 instead of 21.6-21.9. The int4 container and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (vq2 experts) are unchanged there.

The int4 container of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B decodes as 2.1.0 did: 110.0-110.6 tok/s on CUDA (2.1.0: 110.1-111.6), 98.9-99.1 on Vulkan; its prompt reads at 2898-3010 tok/s on CUDA (2.1.0: 2731-2947).

## The setup picks the model for your machine

`coli setup` (START-HERE) used to recommend Qwen3.6-35B on every machine from 12 GB to 512 GB of RAM, card or no card. Now it measures the machine and estimates how fast each model decodes there:
- the RAM's bandwidth, two seconds;
- each card's memory and bandwidth, from the CUDA driver;
- the disk's kind.

It recommends the most capable model that decodes smoothly, at 20 tok/s or more, and the menu shows every model's estimate and where it runs (on the card, half on the card and half in RAM, in RAM, or streaming from the disk). Examples:
- **8 GB laptop:** a 2-bit Inkling-2-Mini.
- **24 GB card:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ3_XXS, about 48 tok/s estimated and 41.5 measured on an RTX PRO 4000.
- **Server with eight H100:** MiMo-V2.6 Pro.

The catalog now has GGUFs too: Inkling-2-Mini and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next from unsloth, imported in place after the download.

## The chat and the API

- `coli web` opens the chat in the browser, with documents (PDF, Word, OpenDocument, PowerPoint, web pages) dropped into a message; the old dashboard is gone.
- `coli tui` is the chat in a terminal: one C file with no libraries, the conversations, the answer with its reasoning folded, the monitor and the expert map. `coli chat` keeps the classic line chat.
- A desktop window (`colibri-desktop`) shows the chat page in a window of its own, starting and stopping the server for you.
- **The prefix store**: every prompt an engine reads is kept by content, and a later request on the same system prompt or the next turn of a conversation takes it with the logits a cold read gives (Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek V4.1, GLM-5.3-Flash, Kimi K3, MiMo, Inkling, OLMoE).
- `tool_choice` naming a function is honored on Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8, MiMo, GLM-5.3 and Mistral-Large-4; `/v1/messages` takes `stop_sequences` and has `count_tokens`.

## Platforms

- A **linux-aarch64** archive (Raspberry Pi 4 and 5, Graviton, Ampere).
- **FreeBSD** x86-64 from source, built with the base system's clang.
- The Windows CUDA package carries every engine with a CUDA path: **glm53.exe, qwen38.exe, deepseek_v41.exe, mimo.exe, inkling.exe, olmoe.exe, laya.exe and gliner_decide.exe** join colibri, qwen36 and kimi_k3.
- `coli setup` builds OLMoE, Laya and GLiNER2.5-Decide with CUDA on an NVIDIA card (OLMoE decodes at 316 tok/s on an RTX PRO 4000, against 32.5 on the CPU).
- **Qwen3.6 on Apple Silicon's GPU** (Metal), from source ([qwen36-metal.md](https://github.com/JustVugg/colibri/blob/v2.2.0/docs/qwen36-metal.md)).
- In a container with a CPU quota or a cpuset, the OpenMP team follows the quota instead of the host's cores (#2914).

## Fixed in this release

- DeepSeek V4 Flash from a GGUF starts on CUDA again (2.1.0 served it; the resident experts' auto mode had refused it since).
- Qwen3.8's RAM plan with its routed experts only in a sidecar (0 cache slots with `Q38_MTP=0`, too many with the MTP head on).
- The grouped int4 kernels' bits on aarch64, where GCC 16 rounded the fused and the single kernels two ways (#2872).
- Qwen3.8's CUDA chain runs the routed experts on the card whenever every one of them is there, whatever the RAM cache's size. With a GGUF that fits the card and `--ram 16`, it had run them all on the CPU (#2966).
- The Windows CUDA package loads its DLL before the chain looks for it, so the chain is no longer "absent" on an FP8 snapshot (#2966).
- On Windows, a GGUF's reads no longer queue one behind the other: on an RTX 5090 with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ1_M, a 4,479-token prompt's first token came in 2.0-2.1 s instead of 5.4-5.8, and the engine was ready in 12.7 s instead of 21 (#2967).
- The expert map (the chat page's and `coli tui`'s) shows where Qwen3.8's experts are on a CUDA card: it had shown every one in RAM or on the disk. It now reads the CUDA tier, and the chain's host pool counts as RAM (#2969).
- Bounds on what the chat takes: an Office file is unpacked up to 64 MB a part and 256 MB in all, a picture is taken up to 8192 x 8192 pixels, and the chat page and the desktop window open links only as http and https.

## For the open reports

- Qwen3.6 on 8 GB cards (#2733, #2734, #2900): the per-row host pool and the memory the KV mirrors give back (#2741), the RAM plan as the engine holds it (#2904).
- A CUDA step that hung on Windows (#2696): the hybrid wait bounded (#2699) and the WDDM flush (#2718).
- A shorter conversation that never reused its prefix with `--kv-slots 1` (#2703), in every engine (#2713, #2718).
- FP8 and int4-g64 experts on a CPU without FMA (#2715): #2724.

Please tell us on those issues whether this release changes what you saw.

**Highlights**

- OmniVoice GGUF uses AMD, Intel and NVIDIA GPUs through Vulkan on Windows and Linux, and Intel Arc GPUs run OmniVoice
- Setup falls back to a smaller CPU build when PyTorch downloads fail, and the app falls back to the CPU when the GPU fails
- Windows loads models one file at a time, and an engine crash names its cause and offers Restart on CPU
- dots.tts voice cloning runs on Windows through audio.cpp, with no Python setup
- Convert can keep your delivery and takes video; Dubbing exports subtitles first and moves lines between speakers

**OmniVoice now uses your AMD, Intel or NVIDIA GPU, and VoiceStudio gets much harder to break.** OmniVoice GGUF runs on any Vulkan GPU on Windows and Linux, sizes its model to your card and can stay loaded between requests (opt-in, Settings → Performance), and Intel Arc GPUs run OmniVoice too. When something goes wrong, the app now keeps going: setup offers a much smaller CPU build when the PyTorch download keeps failing, retries stalled downloads, and VoiceStudio moves to the CPU with a notice when the GPU fails. On Windows, models load one file at a time to avoid a crash on first launch, and an engine crash names the library behind it and offers Restart on CPU.

This release also brings dots.tts voice cloning to Windows with no Python setup, Convert that keeps your delivery and takes video, dubbing that exports subtitles first and moves lines between speakers, a `voicestudio` terminal command, background updates, a new macOS installer window, and hundreds of fixes to dubbing, setup, audiobooks and the phone apps.

Run the new Inkling 2 Mini model, the strongest 26.4B model that runs on 16GB RAM.
This release makes image generation faster and lighter on small GPUs. Macs with Apple Silicon can now restyle videos, and chats that use MCP tools no longer reprocess the whole conversation on every message.

## Highlights

- **Inkling 2 Mini** - less memory usage and faster. New 26B (5.4 active) 1M context - [Guide](https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/inkling-2-mini)
- **MiniMax-H3-Image on 8GB GPUs** renders a new prompt in 36.7 s (prev 82.7 s)
- **GGUF image models load with 52-66% less RAM** on Linux and macOS
- **Video Restyle on Mac** re-renders a whole clip in a new style on Apple
- **MCP chats process 83 to 87% fewer prompt tokens** in our tool tests
- **Scanned PDFs in chat** are now read with OCR
- **Theme files** let you share your Appearance settings

## Images

- FLUX.1 takes 16 to 28% less time per step when its weights stream from system RAM.
- FLUX.3 klein INT8 takes 13% less time per step on T4 GPUs.
- GTX 16xx cards no longer fail image renders with a NaN error.
- Picking a new LoRA on an INT8 or FP8 model offers **Reload and generate** instead of an error.

## Video

- Cosmos3-Edge-FP8 runs about 1.45x faster on L4 GPUs.
- Restyle on Mac needs about 42 GiB of GPU memory for bf16, or 31 GiB for q8_0.

## Diffusion LoRA training

- SDXL LoRA training takes 28 to 31% less time per step on T4 and L4.
- **Auto** precision trains FLUX.2-klein 9B in about 30% less time per step on L4.
- MiniMax-H3 re-runs reuse your encoded dataset.

## Chat + MCP

- A chat keeps its MCP tool list fixed, so each message only processes what is new.
- **Tool output length** in **Settings > Chat** now applies to MCP results on llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama and Custom connections.
- Attached Word files no longer lose moved paragraphs, date fields or furigana text.
- Imported Claude Code and Codex chats keep their images.
- A reasoning model that runs out of tokens while thinking now shows advice and **Retry**.

## Desktop + Mac

- Export or import themes in **Settings > Appearance > Theme file**.
- Unsloth Desktop no longer gets stuck on an incomplete install on some Windows AMD PCs.
- Macs with a chat-only GGUF install no longer show small models as "Does not fit".
- A lost reply during a session refresh no longer signs you out of every tab.

## Training

- AsyncGRPO steps are 1.46x to 2.47x faster on A100 with TRL 1.17 or newer.
- On AMD ROCm, Qwen3.5 training packs sequences by default, about 1.4x the tokens per second on Strix Halo.
- DoRA training is about 3 to 5% faster per step.
- Gemma-4 LoRA training no longer fails on mixed-length batches with PyTorch older than 2.14.
- Dates in JSON and JSONL datasets no longer gain a 00:00:00 time.
- PEFT 0.22 works, and DPO with a PEFT model no longer crashes.

v0.78.0 is a cut of `main` after [v0.77.2](https://github.com/MakazhanAlpamys/Soup/releases/tag/v0.77.2), not a backport: it carries every pull request merged since that tag. By the CHANGELOG count that is 60 additions, 20 changes, 2 deprecations, 171 fixes and 3 security entries. This is not a fixes-only release, and it refuses some input v0.77.2 accepted: a boolean in a numeric `training` field, an enabled eval gate on a path that never ran one, `nan` on six numeric options, an `--output` that is one of `soup ship`'s own inputs, and more. It also changes some numbers: `soup adapters merge` weights, the `tool_call_args_subset` score (which can move a `soup ship` verdict and a `soup eval retention` result), the VRAM pre-flight, and the weights of `classifier`, `reranker`, `cross_encoder` and `asr` runs. Read the upgrade notes under Install / Upgrade before you upgrade a config or a script. Coming from v0.76.x or older, read the [v0.77.0 notes](https://github.com/MakazhanAlpamys/Soup/releases/tag/v0.77.0) first and run:

```bash
soup doctor --config soup.yaml
```

Every user-visible change, with its pull request, is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/MakazhanAlpamys/Soup/blob/v0.78.0/CHANGELOG.md), section `[0.78.0]`; the 33 pull requests that change only tests, CI, documentation, benchmark records or the wording of docs and field descriptions have no entry. Compare with the previous release: [v0.77.2...v0.78.0](https://github.com/MakazhanAlpamys/Soup/compare/v0.77.2...v0.78.0).

## What's New

### Added

- **A continual-learning loop** (#2897, which folded 17 stacked pull requests into one). `soup serve` gives every `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` answer a `response_id` (also the `X-Response-Id` header), `--trace-log` writes one v1 conversation record per answer, and `--feedback-log` turns on `POST /v1/feedback` (thumb, rating, edit or comment, by id) (#2532); `soup serve --adapter-dir` with `POST /v1/adapters/load` loads a LoRA adapter into a running server without a restart (#2516). `soup loop` learns from thumbs, ratings and edits with sft (the new default), dpo or kto (#2538, #2560), paraphrases the prompts people corrected (#2573), judges a candidate with `soup ship --gate loop-v2` by the corrections it learned (#2570, #2588), starts a canary at 5% of keyed traffic and withdraws it when people rate it worse (#2518, #2539), and writes iteration, version and progress logs (#2554). New: `soup loop set` and `soup loop rollback`, `soup loop watch --detach` with a PID file and a log (#2540), `soup ship --base-adapter` to compare two adapters (#2511), and a `soup loop canary` that refuses an adapter whose last verdict was DON'T SHIP, named or given as the path of its directory under `.soup-loops/adapters` (`--allow-dont-ship` overrides it and the override is recorded; #3002). The six JSONL formats are defined in `docs/loop-formats.md` with JSON Schemas (#2505).
- **`soup ship` shows what its number is made of** (#2870, #2894, #2831, #2933). Per task it counts the rows that got better, worse and stayed the same, the answers cut off at the token limit and the failed generations; `--output verdict.json` also writes a per-row audit file `verdict.task-rows.jsonl`; it prints how much of the base the adapter's update changes; a verdict or evidence file carries `schema_version: 2` when it holds any of this detail; a file with none of it has no `schema_version`, which means 1. `--task-mode reward --reward-fn <accuracy|format|verifiable:math|verifiable:json_schema|path.py>` scores each answer with a function from 0 to 1; a `.py` file is executed with your permissions, only when named, and its hash is recorded.
- **Layer streaming does more.** A forward-only inference mode built from an existing shard cache, with adapter reload (`soup_cli.utils.stream_inference`, #2509, #2510, #2636); a pre-quantised bitsandbytes NF4 checkpoint imports byte for byte and trains under `stream_layers: true` (#2628, #2653); BCO and IPO train on a streamed base (#2896, #2915), and so does `task: preference` with a single dpo, orpo, simpo, bco or ipo loss (#2843, #2896, #2915; a `preference_loss_weights` blend is refused, #2766); a checkpointed NF4 layer switches to a packed-state backward when the pre-flight predicts the dense one would not fit (#2655); on Windows the disk tier's page-locked staging checks system commit headroom first (#2658); `soup prune-layer-cache` removes stale cache slots, and the disk pre-flight lists them (#2647).
- **More on Apple Silicon.** Native MLX chat (`soup chat --backend mlx`, #2123), fusion into a standalone dense checkpoint (`soup merge --backend mlx`, #2124), selective per-message loss masks (#2128), consumption of existing preprocessing caches (#2131), vocabulary expansion with trainable new tokens (#2684), linear RoPE extension (#2710) and dense Llama SFT (#2818).
- **New commands and flags.** `soup eval retention` measures forgetting across a series of model versions against a stored record of pinned control tasks, the file named by `--ledger` (#2552); `soup data leakage` reports exact input-text overlap between training and evaluation rows (#2833); `soup docs search` searches the bundled guides offline (#2716); `soup eval quant-check --performance` adds latency, tokens per second and peak memory (#2689); `soup export --format onnx --validate-onnx` compares an ONNX graph's logits with its source (#2695); `soup diagnose --evidence --require-all-modes` (#2857); `soup deploy hf-space` can pick a hardware tier (#2815).
- **Training and tracking.** The experiment tracker records a GRPO run's per-step score and its spread beside the loss (#2891), the live panel shows zero-spread groups (#2819) and the estimated finish time (#2707), runs record the project's Git commit and clean/dirty state (#2692), and `soup runs compare` shows full config differences and the latest stored evaluation scores (#2706). `task: classifier` reports accuracy and F1 (#2789), and `reranker` and `cross_encoder` report ranking quality when validation rows carry `query_id` (#2637).
- **Eight recipes** (181 in all): `qwen3.5-4b-grpo`, `qwen3.5-27b-grpo`, `qwen3.5-122b-a10b-dpo`, `qwen3.5-122b-a10b-grpo`, `qwen3.5-397b-a17b-grpo`, `minimax-m3-dpo`, `qwen3.5-9b-pretrain` and `qwen3.5-2b-pretrain` (#2522, #2605, #2606, #2660, #2718, #2719, #2720, #2721).
- **A library of Triton kernels for the Qwen2 QLoRA SFT step**, `soup_cli.kernels.packed_lora` (#2623). It has no config key and nothing in `soup train` reads it yet. Also: a guarded resident route for Kimi-K2-Base and -Instruct on transformers 5.x (#2759), `soup doctor` prints an NF4 rounding note under an RTX 50-series card (#2587).

### Changed

- **`soup loop` defaults and rules** (#2560, #2539, #2532): `soup loop init` makes an sft loop; a canary is judged by the ratings on its answers with a significance test; `soup serve` refuses `--trace-log`, `--record-thumbs` and `--feedback-log` on the vLLM, SGLang and MII backends instead of ignoring them; a `--trace-log` line has a new shape.
- **The VRAM pre-flight prices differently.** Padded SFT runs are priced by their longest row, so runs it refused because of `data.max_length` now start (#2934); 8-bit runs with checkpointing are charged for what bitsandbytes keeps (#2925); layer streaming is charged its cuBLAS workspaces (#2749); a `task: distill` run is priced with its teacher (#2950); `soup_cli.utils.profiler.profile_from_config` takes `seq_len` and `shape` for programs that call it (#2871); `soup profile` and the MCP `profile` tool do not pass them and still price at `data.max_length`, and `soup profile --model` has its own `--seq`.
- **Resident 4-bit and 8-bit runs on a bf16 card keep embeddings, norms and an untied head in bf16** instead of fp32 (#2683). The record `benchmarks/gate-2609-kbit-fp32-ab.md` (step 1 of #2609: one RTX 4090, Qwen2.5-7B NF4, LoRA r16, 8 x 512 tokens, three seeds, the cast applied through a harness wrapper, not through the shipped helper) measured the unprofiled step 24.9% shorter (2.256 s to 1.695 s) and the allocator peak 3.8 GiB lower (17,425 to 13,520 MiB), with the loss inside a tolerance written before the run. The record's own status is PARTIAL: the cast removed 63.7% of the elementwise gap against a 70% bar and none of the 7,128 MiB of fp32 logits tensors. 8-bit runs, tied embeddings, other model families and other cards were not measured.
- **`soup train --push-as` creates the repository private; `--push-public` keeps it public** (#2802). `soup train --cloud` refuses a config whose local files cannot be shipped (#2627). `soup serve --max-tokens` above 16384 exits 2 (#2898). `training.vllm_sleep_mode: true` is refused on `task: grpo` (#2773). The `mlx` extra needs `mlx>=0.31.2` (#2779).
- **Numbers that moved.** `soup adapters merge` scales each input's term by its weight instead of its square (#2927); `scoring: "tool_call_args_subset"` counts Correct only at full credit (#2939); DPO, ORPO and MLX preference training cut a prompt only when the row overflows (#2555, #2659); `soup runs compare` shows more (#2706); judge task rows are validated before any generation (#2881).

### Deprecated

- `training.warmup_auto: true` and a `training.forgetting_threshold` away from `0.1` load with a warning and are refused in v0.79.0 (#2814). `soup deploy hf-space` with the Streamlit template prints a deprecation warning (#2834).

### Fixed: the ones that matter most

- **Config and options are checked where they are read.** Booleans in numeric `training` and `training.lora` fields (#2462; the numbers of `training.eval_gate`, such as `every_n_epochs`, still accept `true`), wrong-typed values in 38 `training` fields (#2382), integers past the float range (#2912, #2748, #2838), `nan` on six ranged options (#2917), and an unknown key with no close match now names a next step (#1823). The eval gate refuses a suite that cannot load, a repeated key, a boolean threshold, `baseline: previous` and an unsupported path instead of training without it (#2264, #2873, #2697, #2640, #2564).
- **Training.** `soup train --deepspeed` no longer stops before the first step under fp16 (#2276); `task: classifier`, `reranker`, `cross_encoder` and `asr` full fine-tune on fp32 master weights, where 16-bit weights barely moved at the default learning rate (#2949); `training.curriculum: true` trains in sorted order (#2924); fp16 `auto_mixed_precision` loads the frozen base in fp16 (#2921); the BOS token survives a prompt cut in KTO, BCO, ORPO and SimPO (#2544, #2561, #2572); Ctrl+C and `.checkpoint_now` save at an optimizer-step boundary (#2414); `soup train --resume` on `task: ppo` is refused instead of restarting from step 0 (#2772); the GRPO watchdog names the parameters whose gradient was not finite (#2645); `soup sweep` applies the quantization guard of `soup train` and binds each arm to its base revision (#2665, #2799, #2671).
- **Eval, ship and serve.** `soup serve --backend transformers` honours `stop` and `stop_sequences` and streams while it generates (#2630, #2514); `--max-tokens` is bounded on `soup serve`, `soup chat` and `soup bench infer` (#2855, #2898, #2787, #2788); `soup ship` evaluates in native bf16 or fp16 for the requested card (#2669); judge and calibration inputs are checked: finite scores and weights, no duplicate criteria, no empty calibration (#2693, #2701, #2699, #2513); `soup drift-alarm` refuses an input with no tokens instead of saying OK (#2955).
- **No silent overwrites, empty results or crashes.** `soup airgap-bundle` checks size and paths before reading (#2568, #2690); `soup adapters merge` refuses adapters it cannot merge (#2926); `soup data sample`, `soup data mix --apply` (invalid YAML and non-numeric weights), `soup iterative-dpo`, `soup tokenizer train` and `soup expect` report bad input instead of crashing or writing nothing useful (#2931, #2905, #2946, #2958, #2947, #2945); `soup ship` refuses an `--output` that is one of its inputs (#2894); files starting with a UTF-8 byte-order mark keep their first record in `soup drift-alarm`, `soup prune-prompt`, `soup distill-prompt`, `soup iterative-dpo` and `soup data active-sample` (#2901, #2902, #2959, #2943, #2879).
- **Hub, cloud and export.** RunPod jobs use REST API v2, because RunPod announced the retirement of REST API v1 for 2026-11-15 (#2877); the built-in Gradio and Streamlit Space templates no longer raise `TypeError` and publish in one commit (#2657, #2641, #2649); Qwen3.5 GGUF export works on a fresh checkout after the llama.cpp pin moved to `b12423` (#2910); `soup export --format torchao` merges the adapter first (#2920); `soup merge --low-memory` fetches the files and shards a Hub base needs (#2267, #2900).
- **Text shown as typed.** More than 30 pull requests make the commands print paths, names and messages as typed: brackets and `:name:` text are kept and terminal control characters are removed from the display only. What is left is under Known Limitations.

The measurement records behind this release are in `benchmarks/` (42 new Markdown files under `benchmarks/`: 29 measurement records at the top level, each named in `benchmarks/README.md`, and 13 protocol, rule and fixture notes in subfolders; the index is `benchmarks/README.md`). The pre-flight memory estimate changed in v0.78.0 (#2749, #2871, #2934), so the preprint's validation describes the estimator of v0.77.x.

## Install / Upgrade

```bash
pip install -U soup-cli               # or: pipx upgrade soup-cli
soup --version                        # soup v0.78.0
soup doctor --config soup.yaml        # before the first run of an existing config
```

- **From v0.77.2:** a valid `soup.yaml` loads unless it sets a boolean in a numeric `training` field or one of the other values listed first in the upgrade notes; the notes list the rest.
- **From v0.76.x or older:** read the v0.77.0 notes first. Python 3.10 stays on v0.76.x (`pip install "soup-cli[train]<0.77"`). This release supports Python 3.11 to 3.13. v0.76.x gets no further security fixes after this release.
- **Docker:** `docker pull ghcr.io/makazhanalpamys/soup:0.78.0` (also `latest`); the host driver must support CUDA 12.8.

### Upgrade notes

A `soup.yaml` that loads on 0.77.2 loads on 0.78.0, except for the values listed in the first item (refused now). Coming from 0.76.x or older, read the 0.77.0 and 0.77.2 upgrade notes below first, and run `soup doctor --config soup.yaml` before the first run of an existing config.

- **Config values that loaded on 0.77.2 and are refused now.** Each message names the field and what to change.
  - A boolean in a numeric field of `training` or `training.lora` (`lr: true`, `batch_size: true`, `lora.r: false`): 0.77.2 coerced `false` to `0` and `true` to `1`; 0.78.0 refuses it with `<field> must be a number, not a bool` (or `an int`). Write the number you meant (#2462).
  - `training.vllm_sleep_mode: true` on `task: grpo`: it never reached a vLLM engine; delete the line (#2773).
  - `training.eval_gate.enabled: true` (or `--gate`) on `backend: mlx` and on `task: prm`, `unlearn`, `moe_lora_routing`: these paths never attached a gate and trained without one; set `enabled: false` or remove the block, and run `soup eval` or `soup ship` after training instead (#2564). A `training.eval_gate.suite` that cannot load now stops `soup train` with exit 1 instead of training without a gate: fix the suite file the message names, or disable the gate (#2264). `soup train --dry-run` finds it; `soup doctor --config` does not load the suite. `training.eval_gate.baseline: previous` is refused; use a path to a baseline results file (#2640).
  - Eval suites and rubrics: a boolean `threshold`, a repeated key in a task mapping, duplicate rubric criterion names and a non-finite rub
